fails_if: `_cmd_prepare_sources` (cli.py) broadens its wrap to a RegMetaError (say `except Exception`), so the first run reports the located scb_native_id_invalid refusal as source_preparation_failed; or stops wrapping a plain ValueError, so the second run's existing-output refusal reaches the top level as internal_error (exit 30)
note: The CLI mapping the `cases/prepare` readers' refusals are reported under, asserted at the command instead of re-typed in that runner. Run 1 prepares a bundle whose Registerinformation row carries the non-numeric RegVerID `v1` into a new directory and writes its error envelope with `--output`. Run 2 prepares the same bundle into `prepared/`, which already exists, so `prepare_catalog_sources` refuses with a PreparedCatalogError, a plain ValueError, before it reads the bundle. A bundle-level reader refusal (LISA, code list, SOS, curated TOML) cannot reach this command: bundle capture runs those readers and refuses the bundle first. An SCB value-file refusal reaches it as source_preparation_failed, because `prepare_source_values` wraps every ValueError as `cannot prepare source values`.
